States men's Olympic basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Damian Lamonte Ollie Lillard Sr.''' (born July 15, 1990{{cite news|title=Damian Lillard NBA.com profile|url=https://stats.nba.com/player/203081/|website=NBA.com|access-date=November 3, 2019|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191103231816/https://stats.nba.com/player/203081/|archive-date=November 3, 2019}}) is an American rapper and professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He also serves as the [[General manager (sports)|general manager]] of the [[Weber State Wildcats men's basketball]] program in the [[Big Sky Conference]]. Nicknamed "'''Dame Time'''", he played [[college basketball]] for Weber State and earned third-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] honors in 2012. Lillard was selected by the Trail Blazers with the sixth overall pick in the [[2012 NBA draft]] and was named the [[NBA Rookie of the Year]] for the [[2012–13 NBA season|2012–13 season]]. He is a nine-time [[NBA All-Star]], a seven-time [[All-NBA Team]] selection, and the Trail Blazers’ [[List of NBA franchise career scoring leaders|all-time leading scorer]]. As of the end of the 2025–26 season, he ranked fifth on the NBA's [[List of NBA career 3-point scoring leaders|all-time list of three-point field goals made]], with 2,804. In 2021, Lillard won a gold medal for the [[2020 United States men's Olympic basketball team|U.S. Olympic team]] in the [[2020 Summer Olympics]]. That same year, he was named to the [[NBA 75th Anniversary Team]]. In 2023, after a trade request, he was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. In his first season with Milwaukee, he was named the [[NBA All-Star Game Kobe Bryant Most Valuable Player Award|All-Star Game MVP]] and later won the [[NBA Cup]] in 2024. After suffering an Achilles injury during the 2025 playoffs, Lillard was released by the Bucks after two seasons and subsequently rejoined the Trail Blazers on a three-year deal. Outside of basketball, Lillard is also a rapper, under the [[stage name]] '''Dame D.O.L.L.A.''' == High school career == Lillard began his high school career at [[Arroyo High School (San Lorenzo, California)|Arroyo High School]] in [[San Lorenzo, California]],{{Cite web |last=Eggers |first=Kerry |date=April 7, 2016 |title=Damian Lillard: The Face of the Blazers |url=https://pamplinmedia.com/pt/12-sports/301038-177808-damian-lillard-the-face-of-the-blazers |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210125224715/https://pamplinmedia.com/pt/12-sports/301038-177808-damian-lillard-the-face-of-the-blazers |archive-date=January 25, 2021 |access-date=September 10, 2020 |website=Portland Tribune}} and joined the varsity starting lineup as a {{height|ft=5|in=5}} freshman.{{Cite web |last=Buckner |first=Candace |date=January 10, 2013 |title=Blazers' Lillard is just a little kid from Oaktown |url=https://www.columbian.com/news/2013/jan/10/damian-lillard-portland-trailblazers-from-oaktown/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201102231725/https://www.columbian.com/news/2013/jan/10/damian-lillard-portland-trailblazers-from-oaktown/ |archive-date=November 2, 2020 |access-date=August 16, 2020 |website=The Columbian}} He sought to transfer when his coach did not return to the team. For his sophomore year, Lillard transferred to [[St. Joseph Notre Dame High School]] in [[Alameda, California]], the same private school that had produced former NBA point guard [[Jason Kidd]]; but by year's end, a lack of playing time prompted Lillard to transfer schools yet again. He went on to play for coach Orlando Watkins at [[Oakland High School (Oakland, California)|Oakland High School]], where he was First Team All-League his junior and senior years. Over his junior campaign, Lillard averaged 19.4 points a night.{{Cite web |date=January 8, 2014 |title=Damian Lillard's high school coach saw the skill and chip |url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/jpT85Er8S0qOer0QJS59ww/damian-lillards-high-school-coach-saw-the-skill-and-chip.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140109013106/http://www.maxpreps.com/news/jpT85Er8S0qOer0QJS59ww/damian-lillards-high-school-coach-saw-the-skill-and-chip.htm |archive-date=January 9, 2014 |access-date=January 1, 2013 |publisher=MaxPreps.com}} As a senior, he averaged 22.4 points and 5.2 assists per game while leading the Oakland Wildcats to a 23–9 record. Lillard averaged 11.5 points per game and was named the [[Big Sky Conference]] Freshman of the Year and first-team All-Big Sky. In his sophomore year, he raised his scoring average to 19.9 points per game and led the Wildcats to the conference championship. At the end of the season, Lillard was named [[Big Sky Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big Sky Player of the Year]] as well as honorable mention [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] by the [[Associated Press]].{{Cite web |title=Damian Lillard Named 2009–10 Big Sky MVP |url=http://www.weberstatesports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=99544&SPID=3470&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=8600&ATCLID=204900334 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140512231952/http://www.weberstatesports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=99544&SPID=3470&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=8600&ATCLID=204900334 |archive-date=May 12, 2014 |access-date=December 14, 2011 |publisher=weberstatesports.com}} In [[2010–11 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2010–11]], Lillard led the Big Sky in scoring with 19.7 points per contest before suffering a foot injury ten games into the season that forced him to take a medical [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] and sidelined him for the rest of the year.{{Cite web |title=Lillard gets medical redshirt; Wildcat star's junior season restored |url=http://www.standard.net/topics/sports/2011/06/02/lillard-gets-medical-redshirt-wildcat-stars-junior-season-restored |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110901133257/http://www.standard.net/topics/sports/2011/06/02/lillard-gets-medical-redshirt-wildcat-stars-junior-season-restored |archive-date=September 1, 2011 |access-date=December 14, 2011 |publisher=standard.net}} As a redshirt junior, Lillard averaged 24.5 points and led the nation in scoring throughout most of the year but ended up finishing second to [[Oakland University]]'s [[Reggie Hamilton (basketball)|Reggie Hamilton]]. On December 3, 2011, against [[San Jose State Spartans men's basketball|San Jose State]], Lillard scored a college career-high 41 points, including a game-clinching [[three-point play]] to give Weber State a 91–89 double-overtime win.{{Cite news |date=December 3, 2011 |title=Weber St. 91, San Jose St. 89 |work=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=313372692 |url-status=dead |access-date=October 15, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190413171416/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=313372692 |archive-date=April 13, 2019}} At the end of the year, he was named to his third first-team all-conference selection and won his second Big Sky Player of the Year award. Lillard was also a finalist for the [[Bob Cousy Award]].{{Cite web |title=Big Sky Conference – Lillard Among Cousy Final Five |url=http://www2.bigskyconf.com/news/2012/3/9/MBB_0309124949.aspx?path=mbball |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141027095047/http://www2.bigskyconf.com/news/2012/3/9/MBB_0309124949.aspx?path=mbball |archive-date=October 27, 2014 |access-date=January 1, 2013 |publisher=.bigskyconf.com}} Widely regarded as the top point guard prospect in the country, Lillard decided to skip his senior season to enter the [[2012 NBA draft]].{{Cite web |title=Big Sky Conference – Lillard Declares for NBA Draft |url=http://www2.bigskyconf.com/news/2012/4/3/MBB_0403123109.aspx?path=mbball |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141027091810/http://www2.bigskyconf.com/news/2012/4/3/MBB_0403123109.aspx?path=mbball |archive-date=October 27, 2014 |access-date=January 1, 2013 |publisher=.bigskyconf.com}} He finished his college career as the No. 2 scorer in [[Weber State Wildcats men's basketball statistical leaders|Weber State history]] (1,934 points) and the No. 5 scorer in [[Big Sky Conference|Big Sky]] history. He completed his degree in professional sales from Weber State University in May 2015.{{Cite web |date=May 3, 2015 |title=Trail Blazers' Damian Lillard receives college degree – Yahoo Sports |url=http://sports.yahoo.com/news/trail-blazers-damian-lillard-receives-college-degree-204450639--nba.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150503210849/http://sports.yahoo.com/news/trail-blazers-damian-lillard-receives-college-degree-204450639--nba.html |archive-date=May 3, 2015 |access-date=February 16, 2022}} == Professional career == === Portland Trail Blazers (2012–2023) === ==== 2012–13 season: Rookie of the Year ==== [[File:Damian Lillard shoots over Draymond Green.jpg|thumb|right|Lillard attempts a jump shot over fellow rookie [[Draymond Green]] with the Trail Blazers in January 2013.]] Lillard was selected with the sixth overall pick in the [[2012 NBA draft]] by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. In the season opener against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] on October 31, Lillard recorded 23 points and 11 assists to join [[Oscar Robertson]] and [[Allen Iverson]] as the only players in NBA history with at least 20 points and 10 assists in their NBA debut. In addition, his 11 assists were the most by an NBA rookie in his first game since [[Jason Kidd]] (11) in 1994, and the most ever by a Trail Blazer in his NBA debut. Lillard made a career-high 15 field goals and a Trail Blazer rookie-record seven 3-pointers on January 11 against the [[Golden State Warriors]], where he finished with 37 points, six rebounds, and four assists. He became the first Trail Blazer to win an event at the [[NBA All-Star Weekend]], winning the [[NBA All-Star Weekend Skills Challenge|Skills Challenge]]. He also participated in the [[Rising Stars Challenge]] during [[2013 NBA All-Star Game|All-Star weekend]] and finished with 18 points, three rebounds and five assists in a game-high 28 minutes. Lillard became the first NBA rookie to record 35 points, nine assists and zero turnovers in a game since turnovers became a stat in 1978–79 against the [[San Antonio Spurs]] on March 8. On April 10 against the Lakers, Lillard scored a season-high 38 points.{{Cite web |title=Damian Lillard 2012–13 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/l/lillada01/gamelog/2013/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190624035557/https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/l/lillada01/gamelog/2013 |archive-date=June 24, 2019 |access-date=January 22, 2018 |website=Basketball-Reference.com}} He earned Western Conference Rookie of the Month honors for every month, becoming one of just eight players to sweep NBA Rookie of the Month honors since the inaugural award in 1981–82. He finished fifth in the NBA in 3-pointers made, 12th in points per game, tied for 16th in assists per game and tied for 23rd in free throw percentage. He was one of 10 NBA players to score 1,500 points, and he led all rookies in scoring (19.0 ppg), assists (6.5 apg), field goals (553) and free throws (271).{{Cite web |title=Damian Lillard stats, details, videos, and news |url=http://www.nba.com/players/damian/lillard/203081 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180125103642/http://www.nba.com/players/damian/lillard/203081 |archive-date=January 25, 2018 |access-date=January 22, 2018 |website=NBA.com}} With averages of 19.0 points, 3.1 rebounds, 6.5 assists, 0.90 steals, and 38.6 minutes in 82 games (all starting), Lillard not only claimed the [[NBA Rookie of the Year Award]] but joined [[Blake Griffin]] (2011), [[David Robinson (basketball)|David Robinson]] (1990), and [[Ralph Sampson]] (1984) as the only unanimous winners.{{Cite web |date=May 2, 2013 |title=Blazers' Lillard named Kia NBA Rookie of the Year |url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/05/01/damian-lillard-kia-rookie-of-the-year.ap/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171223141226/http://www.nba.com/2013/news/05/01/damian-lillard-kia-rookie-of-the-year.ap/ |archive-date=December 23, 2017 |access-date=January 22, 2018 |website=NBA.com}} He also joined [[Oscar Robertson]] and [[Allen Iverson]] as the only rookies in NBA history to tally in excess of 1,500 points and 500 assists for a season. Lillard became the fourth Trail Blazer in franchise history to win [[NBA Rookie of the Year Award|NBA Rookie of the Year]] honors and one of two to ever finish a season with at least 1,500 points and 500 assists (the other being [[Clyde Drexler]] in 1986–87 and 1991–92). Among other distinctions, he broke the all-time NBA rookie record for 3-pointers in a season (185), surpassing [[Stephen Curry]]'s 166 three-pointers in 2009–10; became the Portland franchise leader for most 3-point field goals in a season, breaking [[Damon Stoudamire]]'s record of 181 in 2004–05; and became the first rookie to lead the NBA in total minutes played (3,167) since [[Elvin Hayes]] in 1968–69. ==== 2013–14 season: First All-Star and All-NBA selection ==== In the season opener on October 30, Lillard scored 32 points against the [[Phoenix Suns]]. He had a second 32-point effort on December 7 against the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. On December 17, he had 36 points, 10 assists, and eight rebounds against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. The following day, he had a second straight 36-point effort against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. Portland finished fifth in the Western Conference with a 54–28 record and faced the [[Houston Rockets]] in the first round of the [[2014 NBA playoffs]]. In Game 1 of the series, Lillard recorded 31 points and nine rebounds in his first playoff appearance to help propel Portland to a 122–120 overtime win over Houston.{{Cite web |date=April 20, 2014 |title=Notebook: Trail Blazers 122, Rockets 120 (OT) |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140420/PORHOU/gameinfo.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180120205904/http://www.nba.com/games/20140420/PORHOU/gameinfo.html |archive-date=January 20, 2018 |access-date=January 22, 2018 |website=NBA.com}} In Game 6 of the series, Lillard became the first player to make a buzzer-beating shot to win a playoff series since Utah's [[John Stockton]] against Houston in 1997. Lillard's 3-pointer as time expired gave Portland a 99–98 victory over Houston, as he finished with 25 points to lift the Trail Blazers to their first playoff series win since 2000.{{Cite web |date=May 2, 2014 |title=Notebook: Trail Blazers 99, Rockets 98 |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140502/HOUPOR/gameinfo.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180116104121/http://www.nba.com/games/20140502/HOUPOR/gameinfo.html |archive-date=January 16, 2018 |access-date=January 22, 2018 |website=NBA.com}} * {{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2014/news/05/03/lillard-clutch-shot.ap/|title=Lillard's historic shot rings out in Portland|work=NBA.com|date=May 3, 2014|access-date=January 22, 2018|archive-date=December 2, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151202124757/http://www.nba.com/2014/news/05/03/lillard-clutch-shot.ap/|url-status=live}} The Trail Blazers went on to lose in five games to the [[2014 NBA Finals|eventual NBA champion]] [[San Antonio Spurs]] in the second round. Lillard had a series-best game in Game 4 with a 25-point effort, helping the Trail Blazers win their sole game of the series. At the season's end, Lillard was named to the [[All-NBA Team|All-NBA Third Team]].{{Cite web |date=June 4, 2014 |title=Durant, LeBron headline 2013–14 All-NBA First Team |url=http://www.nba.com/2014/news/06/04/2013-14-all-nba-teams/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140604220936/http://www.nba.com/2014/news/06/04/2013-14-all-nba-teams/ |archive-date=June 4, 2014 |access-date=January 22, 2018 |website=NBA.com}} ==== 2014–15 season: First division title ==== For the third straight season, Lillard started all 82 games for the Trail Blazers. He averaged career highs in points, rebounds, steals, and field goal percentage, but averaged a career-low 34 percent from three-point range. He shot well during the first two months of the season, before struggling with his shot from January onwards.
